s1.syndrome_frame: Systemic illness with hematologic abnormalities and multi-organ involvement
salient_findings: Pancytopenia with abnormal blastoid cells on peripheral smear
Hepatomegaly and splenomegaly with infarction
Bilateral subdural hemorrhages and pleural effusion
Extensive pulmonary consolidation and thrombosis of the celiac artery
Trilineage dysplasia with megaloblastic changes in bone marrow
key_facts: Two weeks of fever, generalized weakness, and vague abdominal pain
Moderate nasal bleeding and headache
2×1 cm submandibular lymph node
Hepatomegaly (7 cm below the costal margin)
Urea 18.8 mmol/L and creatinine 141 µmol/L
Lipase 182 U/L and myoglobin 108 ng/mL
Ferritin >40 000 µg/L and vitamin B12 <111 pmol/L
Normal fibrinogen and triglycerides
Viral serologies were negative
Pancytopenia with hemoglobin 6.4 g/dL, WBC 1.7×10^3/µL, and platelets 2×10^3/µL
Abnormal blastoid cells on peripheral smear with fine nuclear chromatin and coarse basophilic granules
Bone marrow aspirate showed 26% immature metachromatic blasts and trilineage dysplasia

shortlist.label: Acute Myeloid Leukemia
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of abnormal blastoid cells on peripheral smear and bone marrow aspirate showing 26% immature metachromatic blasts

shortlist.label: Myelodysplastic Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Trilineage dysplasia and megaloblastic changes in granulocytes and erythroid precursors on bone marrow aspirate

shortlist.label: Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Erythrophagocytosis demonstrated by histiocytes and atypical cells, along with fever, hepatomegaly, and splenomegaly

shortlist.label: Histiocytic Sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of atypical cells with coarse basophilic granules and erythrophagocytosis, suggesting histiocytic lineage

shortlist.label: Myeloproliferative Neoplasm
shortlist.why_kept: Splenomegaly and hepatomegaly, which can be associated with myeloproliferative neoplasms

shortlist.label: Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemia
shortlist.why_kept: Monocytosis is not explicitly mentioned, but the presence of immature metachromatic blasts and dysplastic changes could suggest a myelomonocytic component

shortlist.label: Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely, the presence of atypical cells with coarse granules could raise consideration for Langerhans cell histiocytosis, especially with systemic involvement

shortlist.label: Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia
shortlist.why_kept: Although the blastoid cells have features more suggestive of myeloid lineage, the presence of pancytopenia and lymph node enlargement keeps ALL in the differential, albeit less likely

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with fever, generalized weakness, and hepatomegaly, along with laboratory findings of pancytopenia, elevated ferritin, and evidence of erythrophagocytosis on bone marrow aspirate, are consistent with Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis. The presence of abnormal blastoid cells and trilineage dysplasia may also be seen in this condition.

rejected.label: Acute Myeloid Leukemia
rejected.why: While the patient has abnormal blasts, the clinical presentation and laboratory findings are more consistent with a diagnosis of Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis.

rejected.label: Myelodysplastic Syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's findings of trilineage dysplasia and pancytopenia could be seen in Myelodysplastic Syndrome, but the presence of erythrophagocytosis and elevated ferritin levels point more towards Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis.

rejected.label: Histiocytic Sarcoma
rejected.why: This condition is a type of cancer that typically presents with a mass or tumor, which is not described in the patient's presentation.

rejected.label: Myeloproliferative Neoplasm
rejected.why: The patient's findings of pancytopenia and trilineage dysplasia are not typical of Myeloproliferative Neoplasm.

rejected.label: Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemia
rejected.why: The patient's presentation with fever, generalized weakness, and hepatomegaly, along with laboratory findings of pancytopenia and elevated ferritin, are not consistent with Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemia.

rejected.label: Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with skin lesions, bone lesions, or other specific findings that are not described in the patient's presentation.

rejected.label: Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia
rejected.why: The patient's findings of abnormal blastoid cells could be seen in Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia, but the presence of erythrophagocytosis and elevated ferritin levels, along with the clinical presentation, are more consistent with Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis.
